transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm here because I've been completely overwhelmed by these constant, intrusive worries that I just can't shake. I feel forced to repeat certain actions, like checking and cleaning, over and over again just to feel safe. It's starting to take over my entire life, and I really need some help.

Do the checking and cleaning feel like rituals you have to do to relieve distress from unwanted thoughts, or is your worry more general and spread across many parts of life? About how much time do these rituals take each day?

Yes, they are definitely repetitive rituals I feel forced to do to ease intense distress from specific thoughts, like fears of contamination or constantly doubting if I locked the doors. I don't have an exact hour count, but carrying out these rituals takes up a massive, exhausting amount of my time every single day.
Do you recognize that these thoughts and rituals are excessive or unreasonable, even though they feel hard to resist?
I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought much about whether they are unreasonable or not. In the moment, they just feel completely necessary to keep myself and others safe, so I just do them.

Outside of the contamination and checking fears, do you also worry excessively about many everyday areas like work, money, health, or family most days? Or are your worries mainly tied to those specific intrusive thoughts?

My worries are almost entirely tied to those specific intrusive thoughts about germs, contamination, and checking things to prevent danger. I don't really experience that same kind of constant, overwhelming worry about general everyday things like work or money. It's really just focused on those specific fears.
How much are these thoughts and rituals interfering with your daily life, like work, relationships, or leaving the house?

I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about how to measure the impact on my work or relationships. I just know that these rituals take up so much of my time that it makes getting through the day feel incredibly exhausting.
How long have you been having these intrusive thoughts and rituals, and have they been present most days during that time?

I'm not quite sure exactly how long this has been going on, as it feels like it has just built up over a long time. I'm also not certain if it happens every single day, but it definitely feels frequent enough to be exhausting.
Did these symptoms start after using any substances or medications, or after a medical or neurological illness? Have you ever had tics or repetitive movements that you couldn’t control?

No, I haven't used any substances or medications, and I haven't had any recent medical or neurological illnesses. I have also never experienced any tics or repetitive movements that I couldn't control.
Do you avoid certain places, objects, or situations because they trigger these contamination or checking fears? If so, what kinds of things do you avoid most?

I'm not quite sure and I haven't really thought about whether I actively avoid specific places or situations. My focus has mostly been on dealing with the intense urges to clean and check things themselves when they happen.
When you fear contamination or danger, do you see those thoughts as unwanted and coming from your own mind, or are you completely convinced they are definitely true even when others disagree?
I'm not quite sure how to explain it, as it's hard to separate the two. I just know that the thoughts make me incredibly anxious, and they feel completely impossible to ignore in the moment.
If someone you trust tells you the door is locked or that something is clean, does that reassure you even briefly, or do you remain certain it’s still unsafe?

Even if someone I trust reassures me, any relief I feel is extremely brief or doesn't happen at all. The doubt quickly takes over, and I still feel an overwhelming, nagging urge to personally check the locks or clean the items myself to feel safe.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent intrusive contamination and checking fears with repetitive cleaning and checking rituals performed to reduce distress. Symptoms are focused on obsessions and compulsions rather than fixed non-bizarre delusions, and reassurance provides at most only brief relief before doubt returns, which is more consistent with OCD. Insight appears limited/uncertain, but poor insight can occur in OCD. Duration and full functional impairment were not precisely established, though the patient describes the symptoms as frequent, time-consuming, and exhausting.
